name: Oxandrolone

chain: Easier to stay lean while dieting
angle.text: Oxandrolone (Anavar) is an oral steroid popular as a mild cutting compound, and some teens ask about it for height. Real trial data exist in burns and wasting, and the height claims conflict with growth studies.

summary: An oral steroid with real clinical trial data in burns and wasting, popular as a mild cutting drug; its height claims conflict with growth studies.
note: Trial benefits are in patients; teen height use contradicts the growth literature; liver and cardiac risks apply.
currentQuick:
Oxandrolone (Anavar) is an oral anabolic steroid made in the 1960s. It has been prescribed to restore weight after burns, trauma and surgery, and some people use it for a lean, dry physique.
Unusually for the category, it has randomised trials in patients showing weight and lean mass benefits. There are no controlled trials in healthy people for appearance. Teen forum posts discuss it for height, but growth studies show faster bone maturation without taller adult height, per an encyclopedic source.
How it works: It activates the androgen receptor, with relatively mild androgenic effect. The 17-alpha-methyl group allows oral use but is tied to liver strain.
Risks and caveats: Class risks include liver toxicity, cardiovascular effects and hormonal suppression. It is US Schedule III and banned in sport, and unregulated products can be contaminated or fake.
deepLead:
Oxandrolone, widely known by the brand name Anavar, is an oral synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) derived from dihydrotestosterone. It carries a 17-alpha-methyl group and a distinctive oxygen atom in its ring, which are associated with strong anabolic effect and comparatively mild androgenic effect.
It has medical uses in promoting weight gain after surgery, chronic infection, severe trauma or burns, offsetting protein loss from long-term corticosteroid use, and in some paediatric conditions. It is also used non-medically for lean mass and a 'cutting' physique, and some young users in looksmaxxing forums discuss it for height.
Unlike most compounds in its class, oxandrolone has substantial randomised trial data, mainly in burns, trauma and wasting, and these indicate effects on weight and lean mass in patients. Controlled trials in healthy people for appearance were not found in the sources reviewed, and the claim that it raises adult height is not supported by the paediatric growth literature as summarised in an encyclopedic source.

name: Stanozolol

angle.text: Stanozolol (Winstrol) is a doping-famous steroid used for a dry, lean look, and forum posters also claim it masculinises the face or aids height. It is approved for hereditary angioedema, and appearance data are limited.

summary: A famous oral/injectable doping steroid for a dry, lean look; it has an approved angioedema use but little appearance data and notable HDL and liver effects.
note: Banned in sport; lowers HDL and can injure the liver; teen height claims unsupported.
currentQuick:
Stanozolol (Winstrol) is an anabolic steroid approved for hereditary angioedema and used in animals. Bodybuilders use it for lean, dry muscle, and it became famous through the 1988 Ben Johnson doping case.
No controlled trial tests it for appearance in healthy people. Teen forum posters ask about it for height, and no studies support that use.
How it works: It activates the androgen receptor and, in angioedema, raises production of C1 inhibitor in the liver. Its 17-alpha-alkyl structure lets it be taken orally.
Risks and caveats: A weight-lifter study found oral stanozolol cut HDL cholesterol sharply; case reports and animal data describe liver injury, and reviews link AAS to cardiac deaths. It is US Schedule III and prohibited in sport.
deepLead:
Stanozolol, known by the brand name Winstrol, is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) derived from dihydrotestosterone. It was developed in the early 1960s, is approved in the United States for prophylaxis of hereditary angioedema, and is also used in veterinary medicine. It is available as an oral tablet and as an injectable preparation.
Outside medicine it is used by athletes and bodybuilders for lean muscle, strength and a dry, defined look, and it became widely known through doping cases, notably the 1988 Olympic disqualification of sprinter Ben Johnson (per an encyclopedic overview). It is one of the most frequently detected anabolic agents in anti-doping testing.
Controlled research on its appearance effects is sparse. Documented studies concern effects on blood lipids in weight lifters, safety signals such as liver injury, and medical uses in angioedema and blood disorders. In looksmaxxing forums it appears mainly in threads by teenagers asking about height, a use for which no supporting studies were found.

name: Boldenone

angle.text: Boldenone (Equipoise) is a veterinary steroid that bodybuilders use for slow, steady muscle gains. It is approved for horses rather than humans, and no human trials of its appearance effects exist.

summary: A horse steroid used by bodybuilders for slow, steady gains; no human trials exist.
note: Veterinary drug; not approved for humans; prohibited in sport; animal studies report organ toxicity.
currentQuick:
Boldenone is an injectable anabolic steroid, best known as Equipoise, a veterinary drug for horses. Bodybuilders use it illicitly for steady muscle gain.
No human trials of boldenone were found. Claims about its effects on appearance rest on user reports and a single encyclopedic overview.
How it works: It is a testosterone analogue that activates the androgen receptor and is reported to boost red blood cell production. Its long-acting ester releases slowly after injection.
Risks and caveats: Animal studies report reproductive, liver, kidney and immune effects. It is not approved for humans in the US and is prohibited in sport.
deepLead:
Boldenone is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS), the 1-dehydro analogue of testosterone. It is used mainly in veterinary medicine, usually as the long-acting undecylenate ester sold as Equipoise, for debilitated horses, and it is not approved for human therapeutic use in the United States.
It is used illicitly by bodybuilders and athletes for steady muscle gain and appetite, and it is a prohibited anabolic agent under anti-doping rules. Human clinical research on boldenone was not found: no trial of it for muscle or appearance appears in the sources reviewed, and information about it comes largely from veterinary use and an AI-generated encyclopedic overview. Evidence for its appearance effects is therefore unproven.

name: Methandienone

chain: Rapid gain in lean mass and fullness
angle.text: Methandienone (Dianabol) is the classic oral bulking steroid in bodybuilding culture, used for fast mass gains, much of it water. Small controlled trials show lean-mass gains, while most claims rest on anecdote.

summary: The classic oral bulking steroid (Dianabol): small controlled trials show lean-mass gain, with liver, blood-pressure and hormonal costs.
note: 17-alpha-alkylated oral steroid with documented liver, blood-pressure and hormonal effects; controlled in many jurisdictions and prohibited in sport.
currentQuick:
Methandienone, sold historically as Dianabol, is an oral anabolic-androgenic steroid taken by strength athletes and bodybuilders to gain muscle mass. On looksmaxxing and bodybuilding forums it is described as the traditional first-choice oral for rapid size gains.
A handful of double-blind crossover trials from the 1970s and early 1980s, mostly in trained men on a high dose, found increases in body weight, lean mass, body potassium and nitrogen. Strength gains were significant in some of these trials and not in others, and some researchers noted that part of the weight gain could be water.
How it works: Methandienone is a synthetic derivative of testosterone that activates the androgen receptor. Trials in trained men reported weight gain confined to the lean part of the body, increases in muscle size and rises in total body potassium and nitrogen, alongside higher cortisol and lower plasma testosterone during use [1][2].
Risks and caveats: Controlled trials and case reports document water retention, raised systolic blood pressure, side effects leading to withdrawal, suppression of natural testosterone and, in a published case, severe cholestatic liver injury with kidney failure in a bodybuilder also using another steroid [3][4][1]. It is a prohibited substance in sport and is legally restricted in many countries.
deepLead:
Methandienone (also spelled metandienone or methandrostenolone, and sold as Dianabol or D-bol) is a synthetic oral anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from testosterone. It was one of the first anabolic steroids widely used by athletes and remains among the best-known in bodybuilding culture, where it is regarded as a traditional oral compound for gaining mass .
Its effects on body composition were studied in several small controlled trials. In double-blind crossover experiments in athletic men given a high daily dose for six weeks, researchers observed weight gain restricted to lean tissue, larger muscle dimensions and increases in body potassium and nitrogen, while strength gains were not always significantly greater than with placebo . A separate crossover trial in weightlifters found greater improvement on the drug than on placebo, together with water retention, a rise in systolic blood pressure and side effects that led three participants to withdraw .
Documented harms include cholestatic liver injury, a possible association with pancreatitis, and suppression of the body's own testosterone production . Within looksmaxxing communities it is mostly discussed as a bulking agent rather than a facial or aesthetic compound; on T Nation it appears in cycle discussions and historical retrospectives.

name: Oxymetholone

chain: Rapid mass, water and muscle fullness
angle.text: Oxymetholone (Anadrol) is an anemia drug that bodybuilders use as a powerful oral bulker for mass and fullness, and some forum posters say it masculinises the face and body. Its liver effects are well documented, while physique trials are almost absent.

summary: Anadrol: an anemia drug that bodybuilders use as a potent oral bulker, with a well-documented liver-toxicity profile and almost no physique trials.
note: 17-alpha-alkylated oral steroid; hepatotoxicity (peliosis hepatis, liver tumours) is documented in medical use.
currentQuick:
Oxymetholone, sold as Anadrol, is an oral anabolic-androgenic steroid approved in some countries for anemias caused by bone-marrow failure. In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as a strong oral for mass and fullness, and some users pair it with injectable testosterone in cycles.
The published research is about its medical use, not its effect on appearance. Hematology reviews describe it, with danazol, as one of the androgens commonly used in inherited marrow failure, and a general-purpose reference text describes lean-mass gains in short-term wasting studies.
How it works: It is a 17-alpha-alkylated derivative of dihydrotestosterone that activates the androgen receptor and also stimulates red-cell production. The alkylation permits oral use but is associated with liver stress.[1][2]
Risks and caveats: Reviews of androgen therapy for marrow failure report virilization and liver toxicity as major adverse events, and case series link oral androgens to peliosis hepatis and liver tumours.[2][3][4] Forum users also discuss unfavourable cholesterol effects and gynecomastia.[5][6] It is a controlled substance in many places and banned in sport.
deepLead:
Oxymetholone (brand names include Anadrol and Anapolon) is a synthetic oral anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from dihydrotestosterone. It is a 17-alpha-alkylated compound, a structural change that allows oral dosing and that is associated with hepatic toxicity. Its medical role has been in anemias due to deficient red-cell production, such as aplastic anemia and Fanconi anemia.
In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities, oxymetholone is mentioned as a potent oral for rapid mass and a full look, often discussed alongside other orals such as methandienone, stanozolol and superdrol, and sometimes in teen or young-adult cycle threads. T Nation posters describe it both as harsh on blood lipids and liver and as having a reputation that is, in their view, heavier than warranted at lower doses.
No published trial located has tested oxymetholone for cosmetic or physique goals in healthy people. The clinical studies that exist concern anemias and related uses and report benefit in a subset of patients alongside virilization and liver toxicity.

name: Drostanolone

angle.text: Drostanolone (Masteron) is an injectable once used against breast cancer, now used by bodybuilders for a dry, hard, lean appearance. Forum posters also discuss its hair and skin effects. No trials examine appearance.

summary: Masteron: a DHT-derived injectable once used against breast cancer and now used by bodybuilders for a dry, hard look, with no appearance trials.
note: Historic breast-cancer drug; forum users raise hair-loss concerns, and its effects on appearance have not been studied.
currentQuick:
Drostanolone, widely known as Masteron, is an injectable anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from dihydrotestosterone. Medically it was tested in the 1960s to 1980s as hormone therapy for advanced breast cancer. In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as an add-on for a lean, dry, hard look and as a way to limit estrogen-related effects.
The only human trials found are in breast cancer. No published study has measured its effect on physique, face or skin in healthy users, so the claims on forums rest on user reports.
How it works: It is a 2-alpha-methyl derivative of DHT, so it activates the androgen receptor and is not converted to estrogen by aromatase. The propionate ester is the usual injectable form.[1][2]
Risks and caveats: Breast-cancer trials judged side effects generally not serious in that setting.[3] Forum users warn about hair loss in those predisposed, since DHT-derived compounds are not blocked by finasteride or dutasteride in their account, and about skin and cardiovascular effects of stacks.[4][5] It is detected in anti-doping controls and prohibited in sport.[6]
deepLead:
Drostanolone (also dromostanolone) is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid that is a 2-alpha-methyl derivative of dihydrotestosterone. It is most often seen as drostanolone propionate, sold historically as Masteril and in bodybuilding circles as Masteron.
Clinically it was evaluated as hormone therapy for advanced breast cancer in randomized trials from 1968 onward, where it was compared with oophorectomy, nandrolone, testolactone, ethinyl estradiol and tamoxifen. In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums, it is discussed for a hard, dry look when lean and as an add-on to testosterone or other compounds.
No study has tested drostanolone for cosmetic outcomes. The human evidence consists of breast-cancer trials and anti-doping research, while community claims about its effect on skin, facial structure, hair and estrogen control come from user reports.

name: Mesterolone

angle.text: Mesterolone (Proviron) is a mild oral DHT derivative used medically for hypogonadism and fertility. Forum users add it for hardness, libido and puberty-maxxing and debate its effect on hair loss. Appearance effects are untested.

summary: Proviron: a mild oral DHT derivative used in medicine for male hypogonadism and fertility, and by forum users as an add-on for hardness and libido; appearance effects are untested.
note: Fertility trials are mixed; forum reports describe small or no physique effects.
currentQuick:
Mesterolone, best known as Proviron, is an oral androgen derived from dihydrotestosterone. Clinically it has been used for male hypogonadism and was tested for male infertility. On looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as a mild add-on to testosterone for libido, a drier look, and, among younger users, as a way to raise DHT, sometimes under the label of puberty maxxing.
No published study has examined mesterolone for muscle, facial or skin appearance. The fertility trials give mixed results, and the one detailed forum self-report on looksmax.org described only small changes.
How it works: Mesterolone is a 1-alpha-methyl derivative of DHT that acts on the androgen receptor and is not aromatized to estrogen; Grokipedia reports high binding to sex-hormone-binding globulin, which forum users cite as the reason it is added to stacks.[1][2]
Risks and caveats: Grokipedia describes a low risk of liver toxicity relative to other oral androgens, but safety data in healthy users are limited to forum reports.[1] Users raise DHT-related concerns such as hair loss and discuss whether use suppresses the natural hormonal axis; a 1974 study measured pituitary-testicular function in normal men.[3][4][5] It is prohibited in sport.
deepLead:
Mesterolone (brand name Proviron) is a synthetic oral androgen derived from dihydrotestosterone with a methyl group at the 1-alpha position. Grokipedia, an AI-generated encyclopedia, describes it as strongly androgenic and weakly anabolic, not aromatizable to estrogen, and associated with a low risk of liver toxicity.
In medicine it has been used for androgen deficiency in men and was trialled for idiopathic male infertility, with inconsistent results: a randomized trial in 40 subfertile men reported higher semen volume and sperm concentration on mesterolone than on placebo, while a separate randomized comparison of six months' treatment found no significant increase in sperm concentration or partner pregnancies. A Cochrane review of androgens for idiopathic oligo/asthenospermia examined mesterolone and testosterone undecanoate among other agents.
On looksmax.org, Proviron is discussed as a mild add-on, a way to raise DHT, and a supposed safe compound for younger users; community opinion is divided. One user's documented trial of Proviron alone reported stronger erections and a slightly drier look with no change in strength or muscle mass.

name: Methyltestosterone

angle.text: Methyltestosterone is an old oral testosterone analogue used medically for hypogonadism and in menopausal hormone therapy. Appearance and bodybuilding use is undocumented in trials and absent from the forum sources reviewed.

summary: An old oral testosterone analogue still used medically for hypogonadism and menopause; appearance and bodybuilding use is undocumented in trials and absent from the forum sources.
note: 17-alpha-alkylated oral androgen; mood and liver effects documented; no appearance trials.
currentQuick:
Methyltestosterone is one of the earliest orally active forms of testosterone. It has been used for male hypogonadism, in women in combination with estrogens for menopausal symptoms, and in hereditary angioedema. It is also a prohibited substance in sport.
For looksmaxxing purposes it has little documented use in the sources reviewed: no trial has tested it for muscle or facial appearance, and no community threads about it were found. The most relevant human study is a 1993 NIH trial in healthy men that measured mood and behavior effects.
How it works: It is testosterone with a methyl group at the 17-alpha position, which allows oral dosing and raises the risk of liver effects. It acts on the androgen receptor; in human neurons it was shown to protect against apoptosis in vitro.[1][2]
Risks and caveats: Reported risks include virilization in women, liver toxicity, mood changes and a drug interaction with cyclosporine.[1][3] In the 1993 NIH trial, healthy men given methyltestosterone for two weeks were assessed for acute mood and behavioral effects.[4] Combination estrogen-methyltestosterone tablets carry a boxed warning about endometrial cancer risk and are Pregnancy Category X.[5]
deepLead:
Methyltestosterone is a synthetic androgen, a 17-alpha-methyl derivative of testosterone that can be taken by mouth. It has been used to treat male hypogonadism, and in women as part of menopausal hormone therapy, usually combined with esterified estrogens.
Controlled trials have tested it in hereditary angioedema, where in a double-blind study of four patients it was associated with fewer attacks, and in menopausal women, where added methyltestosterone improved one test of attention but showed no net change in overall outcome score. A 1993 NIH double-blind crossover trial examined the acute effects of the drug on mood and behavior in 20 healthy men.
No published study located has tested methyltestosterone for muscle, skin, face or other cosmetic outcomes in healthy people, and no community discussion of the compound was found among the forum sources reviewed.

name: Fluoxymesterone

angle.text: Fluoxymesterone (Halotestin) is a strong oral androgen that bodybuilders add for hardness, strength and aggression more than size. Documented trials cover hypogonadism and breast cancer, and none examine appearance.

summary: Halotestin: a strong oral androgen from the 1950s that bodybuilders add for hardness and aggression; documented trials are in breast cancer and hypogonadism, none in appearance.
note: 17-alpha-alkylated oral androgen; liver and mood effects discussed by forum users and in clinical literature.
currentQuick:
Fluoxymesterone, sold as Halotestin, is an oral androgen first described in the 1950s. In medicine it was used for male hypogonadism and delayed puberty, and as palliative hormone therapy for advanced breast cancer. In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as a strong, short-acting oral for strength, hardness and aggression rather than for size.
Published trials of the drug are in breast cancer and anemia, not in physique or facial appearance. One looksmax.org poster described planning a regimen with a growth-hormone secretagogue and asked about liver protection.
How it works: It is a testosterone derivative with a fluorine atom and 17-alpha methyl group that allow oral use and strong androgenic activity; Grokipedia describes it as androgen-receptor mediated with high androgenic potency relative to its anabolic effect.[1][2]
Risks and caveats: Forum users and one literature summary link long-term use of 17-alpha-alkylated androgens such as fluoxymesterone to hepatocellular adenomas, jaundice and lipid changes, and users describe aggression as a reported effect.[3][4][5] Medical use has declined, and US brand production reportedly ceased in 2014.[1]
deepLead:
Fluoxymesterone (brand name Halotestin; also Androxy) is a synthetic oral androgen and anabolic steroid derived from testosterone. A 1957 JAMA article already carried its name, and later literature describes its use as a replacement androgen in hypogonadism and, in women, as hormone therapy for advanced breast cancer.
Randomized trials compared it with or added it to tamoxifen and chemotherapy in metastatic breast cancer, and a trial compared androgens for anemia in hemodialysis patients. Reviews also note that high doses of synthetic androgens including fluoxymesterone are given by athletes.
In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities it is discussed as a potent oral for hardness, strength and drive; users also discuss its liver toxicity and tendency to produce aggression, and one looksmax.org poster described pairing a small dose with MK-677. No published study has tested it for cosmetic or physique outcomes.

name: Methenolone

chain: Lean muscle gained with less water
angle.text: Methenolone (Primobolan) is a mild DHT-derived steroid prized in bodybuilding for lean gains with fewer side effects. Human trials exist in anemia, cancer and rehabilitation, and none address physique.

summary: Primobolan: a mild DHT-derived steroid prized in bodybuilding for lean gains with fewer side effects; human trials exist only in anemia, cancer and rehabilitation.
note: One small stroke-rehabilitation RCT shows thigh-muscle gain; forum claims of mildness are not trial-tested.
currentQuick:
Methenolone (metenolone), sold as Primobolan, is an anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from dihydrotestosterone, available as an oral acetate and an injectable enanthate. In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums it is regarded as a mild compound for lean gains with fewer estrogenic effects.
Controlled studies are medical: a 1979 trial in refractory anemias, 1975 and later work in breast cancer, and a 2011 randomized trial in stroke patients where weekly injections increased thigh muscle area compared with controls. No study has tested it for physique or appearance in healthy people.
How it works: It is a DHT-derived androgen that binds the androgen receptor and promotes protein synthesis; Grokipedia describes the acetate form as limited by first-pass liver metabolism and the enanthate as a long-acting injectable.[1] In the stroke trial, weekly injections for six weeks increased thigh cross-sectional area.[2]
Risks and caveats: Trials in refractory anemia reported negligible side effects, but one randomized trial found more marked anemia and thrombocytopenia in lymphoma patients given methenolone during chemotherapy, and a rat study found worse cirrhosis-like liver changes with methenolone acetate.[3][4][5] A T Nation post reports a user's liver problems; forum users also dispute how harsh it is on lipids.[6][7] It is prohibited in sport.
deepLead:
Methenolone (also metenolone; brand name Primobolan) is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from dihydrotestosterone, available as an oral acetate and an injectable enanthate ester. Grokipedia, an AI-generated encyclopedia, describes it as a relatively mild androgen introduced medically in the early 1960s for anemias and wasting.
Human studies are clinical. A 19-patient trial of Primobolan in refractory anemias reported remissions in some subtypes with negligible side effects; a 1975 study of the enanthate in disseminated breast cancer reported objective remission in 8 of 41 evaluable patients and described the agent as less virilising than testosterone propionate; and a 2011 randomized trial in 26 hemiplegic stroke patients found larger thigh-muscle gains on weekly injections than in controls.
In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing-adjacent communities, methenolone is discussed as a milder, lean-gain compound that some users consider less toxic than other steroids, although posters differ and no controlled study has measured its effects on appearance in healthy users.

name: Trestolone (MENT)

angle.text: On looksmax forums trestolone is discussed as a topical androgen that might remodel the jawline and face, alongside DHT and trenbolone, and as a far stronger anabolic than testosterone for muscle. The facial remodeling idea is based on theory and anecdote; it was studied as a male contraceptive and replacement androgen.

summary: Trestolone (MENT): an experimental potent androgen developed for male contraception and replacement, now floated on looksmax.org as a topical 'facial remodeling' idea with no supporting data.
note: Never approved; the only registered trial found is a blood-pressure study in normal men, and forum facial-androgen ideas are speculative.
currentQuick:
Trestolone, also called MENT (7-alpha-methyl-19-nortestosterone), is an experimental synthetic androgen that was developed for male hormonal contraception and androgen replacement. It has not been approved as a medicine. In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing spaces it is mentioned as a very potent androgen, sometimes called ment.
The only human research located is a registered phase 1 trial of its effects on blood pressure in normal men. On looksmax.org, one thread proposes applying transdermal androgens to the jawline for facial remodeling, a speculative idea that other users challenged and that no study supports.
How it works: Grokipedia describes it as a potent androgen-receptor agonist with progestogenic activity that is not converted to DHT by 5-alpha-reductase and that suppresses gonadotropins; this is the basis for its research as a contraceptive.[1] The looksmax.org claim of local jawline binding is a forum hypothesis.[2]
Risks and caveats: Because it is unapproved, safety knowledge comes from small research studies, including a registered trial of its effect on blood pressure in 68 men.[3] Forum users anticipate acne, skin irritation and more facial hair from the topical idea, and one asked that any tester be someone not prone to acne or baldness.[2]
deepLead:
Trestolone, known in research as MENT, is a synthetic 19-nortestosterone-type androgen with a methyl group at the 7-alpha position. According to Grokipedia, an AI-generated encyclopedia, it was developed in the 1960s and later studied by the Population Council as a candidate for male hormonal contraception and androgen replacement; it has not been approved for medical use.
The registered human research found is a two-part phase 1 study, completed in 2008 to 2009, with an open-label pilot and a randomized placebo-controlled part, assessing the effects of MENT on blood pressure in 68 normal men. Earlier contraceptive and replacement studies are described by Grokipedia but were not independently confirmed.
In looksmaxxing communities, trestolone appears as a very potent androgen. One looksmax.org thread proposes a stack of transdermal DHT, trenbolone and MENT with IGF-1 to remodel the jawline, reasoning that topical androgens would bind receptors locally; replies questioned the reasoning, noting that preventing bone breakdown differs from causing bone growth. No study has tested this.

name: Dimethandrolone undecanoate

angle.text: Forum users speculate that DMAU could become an oral anabolic steroid, since it is a potent androgen taken by mouth. It was developed as a male contraceptive pill and androgen replacement; trials looked at hormone levels and safety, and its effect on muscle or looks in healthy users is untested.

summary: An experimental oral androgen-progestin built as a male contraceptive pill; no human data on muscle or looks.
note: Investigational only; suppresses natural testosterone and estradiol in men.
currentQuick:
Dimethandrolone undecanoate (DMAU) is an experimental oral drug that acts as both an androgen and a progestin. It is being developed mainly as a male contraceptive pill.
Human trials so far are short studies in healthy men looking at safety and hormone suppression. None has tested it for muscle growth or appearance, so its place in looksmaxxing is mostly speculation in forums.
How it works: After ingestion the ester is cleaved to dimethandrolone, which activates androgen and progesterone receptors and is not converted to estrogen by aromatase in laboratory tests. In men it suppresses LH, FSH, testosterone and estradiol.
Risks and caveats: Not approved anywhere. Short trials report hormone suppression, effects on bone turnover markers and metabolic changes; long-term safety is not established. Hormonal male contraceptives as a class face problems with side effects and non-response.
deepLead:
Dimethandrolone undecanoate (DMAU) is an experimental, orally active synthetic androgen with progestational activity. It is an ester prodrug: enzymes in the body cleave off the undecanoate group to release the active compound, dimethandrolone (7alpha,11beta-dimethyl-19-nortestosterone), a 19-nortestosterone derivative . It has been developed mainly as a candidate male hormonal contraceptive and, secondarily, as a possible androgen replacement therapy .
DMAU is not approved anywhere for any use. Published human work consists of early-phase trials in healthy men, which have examined safety, pharmacokinetics, and suppression of testosterone and gonadotropins . No trial has tested it for muscle gain, body composition or other appearance outcomes in people. Its mention in bodybuilding and anabolic steroid forums is mostly as a news item about male contraception or as a hypothetical oral anabolic .

name: Methasterone

angle.text: Sold in the 2000s as Superdrol, methasterone is used by bodybuilders for quick lean muscle gain with little water retention, and some posters claim non-aromatizing steroids add height in teenagers. Its muscle effect rests on user reports and its androgen class; no human trial exists, and the height claim is untested.

summary: An oral designer steroid once sold as the supplement Superdrol; users report fast muscle gain, case reports document liver and kidney injury, and no human trial exists.
note: Controlled substance in the US; case reports of cholestatic jaundice and renal failure.
currentQuick:
Methasterone is a lab-made oral steroid that was sold as a bodybuilding supplement called Superdrol in the 2000s. It was never approved as a medicine.
No human trial has measured its effect on muscle. Claims of fast gains come from forum logs and animal-based assumptions, while published human reports are mostly of liver and kidney problems.
How it works: It is an androgen-receptor agonist derived from dihydrotestosterone, with a 17-alpha methyl group that lets it work when swallowed. Animal assays suggest a high anabolic-to-androgenic ratio, but this has not been tested in humans.
Risks and caveats: Case reports describe cholestatic jaundice, kidney injury and hospitalisation, and a supplement cluster in New York involved liver damage. Users also report suppressed testosterone, gynecomastia and lipid changes. It is a controlled substance in the US and banned in sport.
deepLead:
Methasterone (2alpha,17alpha-dimethyl-5alpha-androstan-17beta-ol-3-one, also called methyldrostanolone) is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from dihydrotestosterone. It was never approved as a medicine. In the 2000s it was sold in the United States under the brand name Superdrol as an over-the-counter bodybuilding supplement and was described by sellers as a prohormone, although forum users and laboratory studies have treated it as an active steroid itself .
No clinical trial of methasterone in humans for muscle gain or any other purpose has been published. Human information consists of case reports of cholestatic jaundice and kidney injury in users, forensic analyses of supplements, and anti-doping metabolism studies . It is a controlled substance in the United States and is on the World Anti-Doping Agency prohibited list .

name: Androstenedione

angle.text: Marketed in the 1990s as a testosterone-booster prohormone, androstenedione is taken by users hoping to convert it into testosterone and build muscle. Trials at ordinary oral doses looked at strength and muscle gains and did not find them; relabelled analogues such as 1-andro followed after bans.

summary: A weak natural androgen once sold as the 90s baseball-era testosterone-booster supplement; trials found no strength or muscle gains at ordinary doses.
note: US Schedule III since 2005; banned in sport; estrogenic and androgenic side effects reported.
currentQuick:
Androstenedione is a hormone the body makes as a step toward testosterone and estrogen. In the 1990s it was sold as a supplement that would raise testosterone and build muscle, and became famous through baseball.
Controlled studies found that ordinary doses did not improve strength, muscle size or fat, and a single large dose raised testosterone only briefly while also raising estradiol.
How it works: It is converted by enzymes to testosterone, or by aromatase to estrone. It is itself only a weak androgen, so any effect depends on how much converts.
Risks and caveats: The 100 mg study in women reported masculinising effects and menstrual disruption. Estrogenic effects are a concern in men. It was banned as a supplement in 2004 and has been a Schedule III controlled substance in the US since 2005; it is banned in major sports.
deepLead:
Androstenedione (androst-4-ene-3,17-dione, often called "andro" or A4) is an endogenous steroid hormone made in the adrenal glands and gonads. It is a weak androgen and an intermediate in the body's synthesis of testosterone and of estrone, and it can be converted in either direction between itself and testosterone . Its level in blood is used as a marker in conditions such as polycystic ovary syndrome and congenital adrenal hyperplasia .
In the 1990s it was sold in the United States as an over-the-counter dietary supplement promoted as a testosterone booster for strength and muscle, and became widely known through its use by professional baseball players . Controlled studies in men reported that low doses did not raise testosterone meaningfully, and a review found no improvement in strength, muscle size or body fat at 50 to 100 mg per day . It is now a Schedule III controlled substance in the US and is banned in most organised sport .

name: DHEA

angle.text: DHEA is taken as a fountain-of-youth supplement for skin and vitality, as a way to raise testosterone, and in some forum posts for height. It is well studied for vaginal atrophy; its use for skin, muscle, or growth in healthy people has thin evidence and rests largely on anecdote.

summary: A natural adrenal hormone sold as an over-the-counter anti-aging and testosterone-support pill; solid for vaginal atrophy, thin for muscle or looks.
note: Sold as a supplement in the US; banned or restricted in some countries and in sport.
currentQuick:
DHEA is a hormone made by the adrenal glands that the body turns into testosterone and estrogen. Levels fall with age, which is why it is sold as an anti-aging and hormone-support supplement.
Trials support the vaginal form for menopausal atrophy. For muscle, skin or looks in healthy people, evidence is limited.
How it works: It acts mostly as a precursor converted in tissues to androgens and estrogens, plus some direct activity in the brain. Its sulfate form, DHEA-S, acts as a long-lasting reservoir.
Risks and caveats: In the US it is sold over the counter, but some countries restrict it and it is prohibited in sport. Because it converts to sex hormones, hormonal effects are possible; users on testosterone therapy report mixed experiences.
deepLead:
Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA, also called androstenolone or prasterone) is an endogenous steroid precursor and one of the most abundant circulating steroids in humans. It is made mainly by the adrenal glands, with smaller amounts from the gonads and brain, and serves as an intermediate in the synthesis of androgens and estrogens; it also has weak direct hormonal and neurosteroid effects . Its sulfate ester, DHEA-S, is a stable marker of adrenal androgen activity .
Blood levels peak around age 20 and fall steadily with age, a pattern called adrenopause. This decline underlies its promotion as an anti-aging and testosterone-supporting supplement . In the United States DHEA is sold over the counter as a supplement and as the prescription product prasterone . Published trials support medical use in some situations such as vaginal atrophy, while evidence for appearance and body composition benefits in healthy people is limited .

name: Dihydrotestosterone (DHT)

chain: Local facial bone and tissue effect
angle.text: DHT gel is promoted on forums for masculinizing the face during puberty, strengthening the jaw, and increasing penile size. DHT is the androgen that drives facial and body hair at puberty, but the facial bone and size claims for applied gel are anecdotal, with no trials in healthy people.

summary: The potent androgen behind puberty and balding; DHT gel is a forum favourite for face and penis claims with no trials in healthy people.
note: Topical DHT gel is not an approved US product; hormone suppression reported by users.
currentQuick:
DHT is a hormone made from testosterone that shapes male genital development and puberty changes, and it is also the hormone behind male-pattern baldness. Forum users apply DHT gel hoping for a more masculine face, beard or penis size.
DHT gel has been studied in older men with low testosterone and used in boys with micropenis, but no trial has tested it for looks in people without a hormonal disorder.
How it works: DHT binds the androgen receptor more strongly than testosterone does and cannot turn into estrogen. Applied as a gel, it is absorbed through the skin and raises DHT in the blood.
Risks and caveats: Users and a forum-cited study describe suppression of the body's own testosterone with DHT gel. Androgens can cause acne and mood changes, and their effect on adolescent growth is unstudied. DHT gel is not an approved US product.
deepLead:
Dihydrotestosterone (DHT, 5alpha-dihydrotestosterone, androstanolone) is an endogenous androgen made from testosterone by the enzyme 5alpha-reductase, mainly in tissues such as the prostate, skin and hair follicles. It binds the androgen receptor more strongly than testosterone and cannot be converted to estrogen by aromatase . It drives development of the male external genitalia in the fetus and, at puberty, facial and body hair, and it is implicated in male-pattern hair loss and prostate enlargement .
In looksmaxxing communities, DHT is discussed in two ways: as something to lower, through 5alpha-reductase inhibitors such as finasteride and dutasteride for hair loss, and as something to apply, in homemade or compounded topical DHT gels that some users say can enhance facial bone masculinisation during puberty, beard growth or penile size . A prescription DHT gel was studied in a phase 2 trial in older men with low testosterone, and topical DHT has been used clinically in boys with micropenis . No published trial has tested topical DHT for facial structure in people without an endocrine disorder.

name: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG)

angle.text: Men on testosterone therapy use hCG to keep the testes active and preserve fertility, and some looksmaxxers add it to growth hormone or DHT gel hoping for facial or penile growth. Its testicular use is established medically; the facial, height, and size claims are untested.

summary: The pregnancy hormone that fertility clinics and TRT doctors use to keep testes working; forum claims for face, height and penis growth are untested.
note: Prescription-only injectable in the US; OTC hCG weight-loss products are unapproved.
currentQuick:
hCG is the hormone made by the placenta that pregnancy tests detect. It mimics luteinizing hormone, so doctors use it to trigger ovulation and to stimulate the testes in some men with hypogonadism.
In looksmaxxing circles it is mainly used by men on testosterone or steroids to keep testes working and fertility intact. Claims for facial growth, height or penis size have not been tested in trials.
How it works: hCG binds the luteinizing hormone receptor. In men this stimulates the testes to make testosterone and supports sperm production, which are otherwise suppressed when outside testosterone shuts down the pituitary signal.
Risks and caveats: It is a prescription injectable in the US; non-prescription hCG weight-loss products are unapproved. Because it raises testosterone and so estradiol, users report needing to monitor hormones. Ovarian hyperstimulation is a known complication in fertility treatment.
deepLead:
Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) is a glycoprotein hormone made by the placenta after implantation, consisting of an alpha subunit shared with other gonadotropins and a hormone-specific beta subunit. It sustains the corpus luteum and progesterone production in early pregnancy and is the basis of pregnancy tests . Because it acts on the luteinizing hormone receptor, it is used as a prescription injectable to trigger ovulation in fertility treatment and to stimulate the testes in some men with low testosterone .
In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities hCG is discussed as an add-on for men using testosterone or anabolic steroids, to maintain testicular size and fertility while the body's own luteinizing hormone signal is suppressed. Some forum posts also propose it for facial masculinity, penile growth or alongside growth hormone for height, uses for which no trial evidence was found . Clinical literature supports hCG for inducing puberty and spermatogenesis in men with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, and reviews list it among options for steroid-induced hypogonadism .

name: Andarine (S-4)

angle.text: Andarine is a SARM that users take during cutting phases to hold onto muscle while losing fat, with posters saying it spares hair compared with steroids. Evidence for that use comes from animal studies and anecdote, and users also report a yellow-green tint to vision.

summary: An unapproved SARM from the early 2000s, known in forums for cutting use and for turning vision yellow-green; only animal data exist.
note: Not approved anywhere; vision disturbances widely reported; banned in sport.
currentQuick:
Andarine (S-4) is an experimental SARM, a drug designed to act like testosterone on muscle and bone with fewer effects elsewhere. It was developed in the early 2000s and never approved.
Only animal studies exist. Forum users take it for cutting and widely mention a side effect of yellow or green tinted vision and poor night vision.
How it works: It binds the androgen receptor, acting as a full agonist in muscle and bone and a partial agonist in the prostate in animal experiments. It is non-steroidal and does not convert to estrogen or DHT.
Risks and caveats: Vision disturbances are widely reported by users. Forum posts also cite unfavourable cholesterol changes and product contamination concerns. It is unapproved, illegal to sell for human consumption in many places, and banned in sport.
deepLead:
Andarine, also known as S-4 and GTx-007, is an investigational, non-steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) of the aryl-propionamide class, structurally derived from the antiandrogen bicalutamide. It was developed in the early 2000s by researchers at the University of Tennessee and GTx, Inc., with the aim of producing the muscle and bone effects of androgens with fewer effects on tissues such as the prostate .
Andarine has not been approved by the US FDA or any other regulator, and the sources reviewed here describe no published human clinical trial of it. Evidence of effect is limited to animal studies, in which it restored muscle mass in castrated rats . It is prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency . In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums it is known mainly for use during cutting phases and for a reported visual side effect, a yellow or green tint and poor night vision .

name: Cardarine (GW501516)

angle.text: Cardarine is used as a fat-loss and endurance aid, often described as a milder alternative to clenbuterol for getting lean. Small trials looked at lipid and metabolic markers rather than appearance, and development stopped after rodent cancer findings.

summary: A discontinued metabolic drug sold as a fat-loss and endurance aid; some lipid benefits in small trials, but rodent cancer findings ended its development.
note: Rodent studies found cancer in several organs; banned in sport; no approved use.
currentQuick:
Cardarine is an experimental drug that activates PPAR-delta, a receptor that turns up fat burning in muscle. GSK developed it for cholesterol and metabolic disease and then stopped in 2007.
Small human trials showed better triglycerides, HDL and fat oxidation, but none was designed to test weight or fat loss in healthy people. It is sold alongside SARMs and used by some in cuts.
How it works: It selectively activates PPAR-delta, which raises expression of genes for fatty acid transport and oxidation in muscle and has been described as mimicking some effects of exercise.
Risks and caveats: Rodent studies found tumour development in several organs, which led GSK to halt research. There are no long-term human safety data. It is banned by WADA and unapproved, and some countries such as Australia have scheduled it.
deepLead:
Cardarine, also known as GW501516, GW-1516 and Endurobol, is an experimental drug that selectively activates the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor delta (PPAR-delta). It was developed by Ligand Pharmaceuticals and GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) as a possible treatment for dyslipidemia and metabolic disease, and GSK stopped development in 2007 . It was later found to cause cancer in several organs in rodents at high doses, according to Wikipedia .
It is not a hormone or a SARM, although it is sold and discussed alongside SARMs. In looksmaxxing forums it is used for fat loss and endurance, mostly in leanmaxxing and cutting plans . Small randomized trials in healthy volunteers and in people with obesity or dyslipidemia reported effects on triglycerides, HDL cholesterol and fat oxidation, while no trial has tested it for appearance outcomes in healthy people . The World Anti-Doping Agency prohibited it in 2009 and warned in 2013 about health risks .

name: SR9009 (Stenabolic)

angle.text: Sold as Stenabolic, SR9009 is used for endurance and cutting, often stacked with cardarine and other compounds. The fat-loss and endurance effects come from mouse studies; human appearance data is absent, and it is not actually a SARM despite being sold alongside them.

summary: A REV-ERB clock-receptor agonist sold as Stenabolic for endurance and cutting; mouse data only, nothing in humans, and a liver-injury case report.
note: Not a SARM despite the label; no human trials; liver injury case reported.
currentQuick:
SR9009 (Stenabolic) is a lab compound that switches on REV-ERB, receptors that tie the body clock to metabolism. It is sold online for endurance and fat loss and is often called a SARM, though research classifies it differently.
All published work is in cells and animals. No human trial has tested it for appearance or performance.
How it works: It activates REV-ERBα and REV-ERBβ, which repress clock and metabolic genes. Several studies report effects that appear independent of REV-ERB, so its mechanism is not settled.
Risks and caveats: Human safety is unestablished. A 2025 case report describes liver injury after starting a product sold as Stenabolic. It is not an approved drug, and users often combine it with other compounds, which confounds any reported effects.
deepLead:
SR9009, sold under the name Stenabolic, is a synthetic small molecule that activates REV-ERB, a pair of nuclear receptors (REV-ERBα and REV-ERBβ) that help run the body's circadian clock and regulate metabolism and inflammation. It was developed as a laboratory tool compound and has been studied in cells and animals; it is not an approved medicine anywhere. 
In bodybuilding and fitness forums it is marketed and discussed as an endurance, fat-loss and "SARM-adjacent" product, often stacked with other research compounds such as Cardarine.  Published research, however, classifies it as a REV-ERB agonist rather than a selective androgen receptor modulator, and the evidence base consists of preclinical studies in rodents and cell lines. 
No published human clinical trial has tested SR9009 for fat loss, endurance or muscle. A 2025 case report described drug-induced liver injury in a man who had started a product sold as Stenabolic, and several studies have reported effects of SR9009 that appear independent of REV-ERB, complicating interpretation of the animal data.
